ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the radius of the drainage pipe's cross-section is 5 decimeters, and the width of the water surface $AB=8$ decimeters, with $OC\perp AB$. What is the maximum depth $CD$ of the water?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since the diameter of circle O is 10 dm,\\
it follows that OA=5 (dm),\\
and since OD$\perp$AB, and AB=8 (dm),\\
it follows that AD=BD=4,\\
hence, OD$=\sqrt{OA^{2}-AD^{2}}=3$,\\
therefore, the maximum depth of the water CD=OC-OD=5-3=\boxed{2} (dm).

method.method_draft: Use the center-to-chord perpendicular triangle. From the image, identify the circular pipe cross-section with center O, water surface AB as a chord, C as the lowest point of the circle, and D as the foot where the vertical line OC meets AB. From the text, take radius OA=OC=5 dm, chord length AB=8 dm, and OC ⟂ AB. Apply the theorem that a perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, so AD=4 dm. Then in right triangle ODA, compute OD=sqrt(OA^2-AD^2)=sqrt(25-16)=3 dm. Since CD is the vertical distance from the water surface chord to the bottom of the circle, CD=OC-OD=5-3=2 dm.
